papers.path: papers/LEASH Logit-Entropy Adaptive Stopping Heuristic for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (arXiv 2511.04654v1).pdf
papers.file: LEASH Logit-Entropy Adaptive Stopping Heuristic for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (arXiv 2511.04654v1).pdf
papers.title: Logit-Entropy Adaptive Stopping Heuristic for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.summary: LEASH is a training-free token-level heuristic that stops a rationale when full-vocabulary entropy slope and top-two log-probability-margin improvement both plateau, subject to a peak-probability saturation guard, entropy-drop gate, warm-up, and majority vote across recent non-saturated steps. It then issues a second prompt for a short final answer. The savings are substantial but accompany about a ten-point accuracy loss, so it is a sensitivity baseline rather than the strongest target.
papers.review_connection: Use the realized stopping lane to show the accuracy cost of saved tokens. Do not turn a token reduction into a detector superiority claim.

papers.path: papers/LOCA - LOcal Conformal Autoencoder.pdf
papers.file: LOCA - LOcal Conformal Autoencoder.pdf
papers.title: LOCA - LOcal Conformal Autoencoder
papers.summary: Abstract We propose a deep-learning based method for obtaining standardized data coordi- nates from scientiﬁc measurements. Data observations are modeled as samples from an unknown, non-linear deformation of an underlying Riemannian manifold, which is parametrized by a few normalized latent variables. By leveraging a repeated measure- ment sampling strategy, we present a method for learning an embedding in Rd that is isometric to the latent variables of the manifold. These data coordinates, being invariant under smooth changes of variables, enable matching between diﬀerent instrumental obser- vations of the same phenomenon. Our embedding is obtained using a LOcal Conformal Autoencoder (LOCA), an algorithm that constructs an embedding to rectify deformations by using a local z-scoring procedure while preserving relevant geometric information. We demonstrate the isometric embedding properties of LOCA on various model settings and observe that it exhibits promising interpolation and extrapolation capabilities. Finally, we apply LOCA to single-site Wi-Fi localization data, and to 3-dimen
papers.review_connection: LOCA seeks standardized coordinates from repeated measurements. Its conformal geometry is not Bracha’s conformal-prediction calibration chapter.

papers.path: papers/Local_Manifold_Explanations.pdf
papers.file: Local_Manifold_Explanations.pdf
papers.title: Local Manifold Explanations with Tangent Space Regression
papers.summary: LTSREx explains the local intrinsic geometry of an already chosen or estimated manifold. At each sample it estimates a tangent space, regresses the local tangent coordinates on a supplied interpretable feature dictionary with ElasticNet, and smooths the resulting coefficient vector fields with a parallel-transport-aware connection Laplacian. LEGO is the paper's robust tangent estimator for normal noise and curvature. The method is an explanation method, not a target-aware manifold-selection method: it assumes a sample manifold/embedding and local dimension, and the authors explicitly leave dictionary choice to domain knowledge. It can explain which variables drive a chosen geometry, but does not determine whether that geometry represents hallucination correctness rather than a nuisance.
papers.review_connection: LTSREx/LEGO explain an already-chosen manifold. They do not supply the missing correctness axis in unlabeled features.

papers.path: papers/LongCoT Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning.pdf
papers.file: LongCoT Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning.pdf
papers.title: LongCoT: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.summary: Benchmarks long-horizon Chain-of-Thought reasoning across extended problem suites requiring extensive generation lengths. Evaluates structural error accumulation across long reasoning trajectories.
papers.review_connection: Long reasoning is relevant to error accumulation. Confirm annotation and task compatibility before treating this benchmark as fresh first-error evaluation.

papers.path: papers/Mind the Gap -  Catching Hallucinations via Evidence Drop on the Reasoning.pdf
papers.file: Mind the Gap -  Catching Hallucinations via Evidence Drop on the Reasoning.pdf
papers.title: Mind the Gap: Catching Hallucinations via Evidence Drop on the Reasoning Manifold
papers.summary: Reasoning is modelled as a trajectory of latent evidence states on a low-dimensional **Evidence Manifold**, evolving as a Markov process. Under two locality assumptions (the training data contains no direct transitions between non-adjacent evidence states; adjacent transitions preserve the true local structure), Theorem 3.1 shows an off-manifold transition drives the optimal predictive distribution to **uniform** — so a hallucination is not high *absolute* uncertainty but a **sudden decline** in evidence. The detector is therefore training-free and single-pass: take negative renormalized top-K entropy as an evidence proxy, EMA-smooth it, and score a trace by the **mean of its M most negative first-differences**. Because the score is built from *located* drops, the same statistic localizes to a reasoning step.
papers.review_connection: A direct trace-based localization comparator. Match top-K, smoothing and score aggregation; distinguish the paper’s SLA/policy from this project’s common-calibration PB F1.

papers.path: papers/Multi-modal Differentiable Unsupervised Feature Selection.pdf
papers.file: Multi-modal Differentiable Unsupervised Feature Selection.pdf
papers.title: Multi-modal Differentiable Unsupervised Feature Selection
papers.summary: Abstract Multi-modal high throughput biological data presents a great scientiﬁc oppor- tunity and a signiﬁcant computational challenge. In multi-modal measurements, every sample is observed simultaneously by two or more sets of sensors. In such settings, many observed variables in both modalities are often nuisance and do not carry information about the phenomenon of interest. Here, we propose a multi-modal unsupervised feature selection framework: identifying informative variables based on coupled high-dimensional measurements. Our method is designed to identify features associated with two types of latent low-dimensional structures: (i) shared structures that govern the observations in both modalities and (ii) diﬀerential structures that appear in only one modality. To that end, we propose two Laplacian-based scoring operators. We incorporate the scores with diﬀerentiable gates that mask nuisance features and enhance the accuracy of the structure captured by the graph Laplacian. The performance of the new scheme is illustrated using synthetic and real datasets, including an extende
papers.review_connection: Shared/private structure requires meaningfully different modalities. Multiple transforms of one entropy trace do not automatically supply independent views.

papers.path: papers/One-Pass Algorithms for MAP Inference of Nonsymmetric Determinantal Point Processes.pdf
papers.file: One-Pass Algorithms for MAP Inference of Nonsymmetric Determinantal Point Processes.pdf
papers.title: One-Pass Algorithms for MAP Inference of Nonsymmetric Determinantal Point Processes
papers.summary: Abstract In this paper, we initiate the study of one-pass algorithms for solving the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) inference problem for Non-symmetric De- terminantal Point Processes (NDPPs). In particu- lar, we formulate streaming and online versions of the problem and provide one-pass algorithms for solving these problems. In our streaming set- ting, data points arrive in an arbitrary order and the algorithms are constrained to use a single-pass over the data as well as sub-linear memory, and only need to output a valid solution at the end of the stream. Our online setting has an additional requirement of maintaining a valid solution at any point in time. We design new one-pass algorithms for these problems and show that they perform comparably to (or even better than) the offline greedy algorithm while using substantially lower memory. 1. Introduction Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs) were first introduced in the context of quantum mechanics (Macchi, 1975) and have subsequently been extensively studied with applica- tions in several areas of pure and applied mathematics like graph
papers.review_connection: DPP diversity selection is a different optimization problem. “One pass” here refers to data streaming, not one LLM generation.

papers.path: papers/Online Auditing of Information Flow.pdf
papers.file: Online Auditing of Information Flow.pdf
papers.title: Online Auditing of Information Flow
papers.summary: Formulates fake-news detection on a social graph as a **sequential (quickest) detection** problem: minimize a joint risk that prices *both* decision error and the delay before deciding. Information spreads along a directed graph as a Markov chain over discretized edge weights `W_e ∈ {0,…,Z−1}`; because only arbitrary parts of a propagation trace are observed, the observed process is a hidden Markov chain. The authors reduce the joint minimization over (stopping time `T`, decision rule `δ`) to a pure optimal-stopping problem on the posterior `Π_ℓ = P(H₁|F_ℓ)` (Thm 2), give the optimal rule as a **two-sided threshold on `Π_ℓ`** solved by a Bellman recursion (Thm 3), and show it is representable as an **SPRT** with Wald-calibrated boundaries (Thm 4, Prop 1). On Weibo they match QuickStop's accuracy in **roughly half the decision time**.
papers.review_connection: Useful framing for the cost of detection delay. Its social-graph stochastic model is not a validated model of an LLM reasoning trace.

papers.path: papers/ProcessBench Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning (arXiv 2412.06559v4).pdf
papers.file: ProcessBench Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning (arXiv 2412.06559v4).pdf
papers.title: PROCESSBENCH: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning
papers.summary: PROCESSBENCH is the canonical first-error localization benchmark used by this project. Each record contains a math problem, a paragraph/step-separated solution, and the zero-based index of the earliest erroneous step, or `-1` when all steps are correct. Its primary metric is the harmonic mean of accuracy on erroneous traces and accuracy on clean traces, called F1 by the paper.
papers.review_connection: Primary benchmark definition: earliest erroneous step or no error. Preserve clean/error accuracy, step indexing, and source-question grouping.

papers.path: papers/RAGTruth A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models.pdf
papers.file: RAGTruth A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models.pdf
papers.title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
papers.summary: Introduces RAGTruth, a large-scale corpus of nearly 18,000 RAG responses generated by diverse LLMs with fine-grained word-level and span-level human hallucination annotations across summarization, QA, and data-to-text tasks.
papers.review_connection: Human-annotated grounding data. Preserve task, source-document groups and response/sentence/token units; do not mix pooled and within-task claims.

papers.path: papers/REVIS_Sparse_Latent_Steering.pdf
papers.file: REVIS_Sparse_Latent_Steering.pdf
papers.title: REVIS: Sparse Latent Steering to Mitigate Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: REVIS is a training-free framework designed to mitigate object hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by re-activating suppressed visual information in the latent space. The authors show that visual features and language priors become entangled in deep layers, leading to visual suppression. REVIS extracts a "pure visual vector" via orthogonal projection (subtracting the language prior direction) and applies sparse latent steering (intervention) only at the specific layer (e.g. layer 27) where visual suppression peaks. This surgical approach reduces object hallucinations while preserving general reasoning.
papers.review_connection: Visual latent steering changes the generation process. Keep outside the current text-only localization paper.

papers.path: papers/Revisiting Hallucination Detection with Effective Rank-based Uncertainty.pdf
papers.file: Revisiting Hallucination Detection with Effective Rank-based Uncertainty.pdf
papers.title: REVISITING HALLUCINATION DETECTION WITH EFFECTIVE RANK-BASED UNCERTAINTY
papers.summary: Proposes effective rank-based uncertainty quantification for hallucination detection, analyzing the spectral rank of hidden state representations and logit covariance across decoding steps.
papers.review_connection: Effective-rank uncertainty uses internal representation structure. Compare matched rows and access; spectral terminology alone does not imply the same method.

papers.path: papers/SELF-SUPERVISION ENHANCED FEATURE SELECTION.pdf
papers.file: SELF-SUPERVISION ENHANCED FEATURE SELECTION.pdf
papers.title: Self-Supervision Enhanced Feature Selection with Correlated Gates
papers.summary: SEFS is a **semi-supervised** embedded feature-selection method for the small-labelled-sample, highly-correlated-feature regime (clinical / omics). Two phases: a **Self-Supervision Phase** pre-trains an encoder on unlabeled data via two pretext tasks — reconstruct the original feature vector, and predict which features were masked — and a **Supervision Phase** that jointly updates the encoder, a predictor and a per-feature selection probability `π` under a supervised loss plus an ℓ0 penalty. Its headline novelty is **correlated gates**: the masking vector is drawn from a multivariate Bernoulli built with a **Gaussian copula** carrying the input features' correlation matrix `R`, so correlated features tend to be masked *together*.
papers.review_connection: The cached audit identifies a supervised phase. “Self-supervision” in the title is not enough to call the full selector label-free.

papers.path: papers/Semantic Energy Detecting LLM Hallucination Beyond Entropy.pdf
papers.file: Semantic Energy Detecting LLM Hallucination Beyond Entropy.pdf
papers.title: Semantic Energy: Detecting LLM Hallucination Beyond Entropy
papers.summary: Proposes Semantic Energy, an energy-based formulation that evaluates probability mass sharpness across semantic clusters of generated responses to detect hallucinations beyond standard token or sequence entropy.
papers.review_connection: Verify the precise source distribution and semantic aggregation before comparison. Do not infer access cost or the formula from the method’s name.

papers.path: papers/Semantic Entropy Probes Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs.pdf
papers.file: Semantic Entropy Probes Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs.pdf
papers.title: Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs
papers.summary: Proposes Semantic Entropy Probes (SEPs), a cheap and reliable method for uncertainty quantification and hallucination detection in LLMs. Approximates Semantic Entropy directly from internal hidden states and log-probabilities at a single generation pass, eliminating the 5x-10x cost of sampling multiple semantic clusters.
papers.review_connection: Single-pass application can hide supervised probe training costs. Report both training and inference access when positioning this method.

papers.path: papers/Semantic Uncertainty Quantification of Hallucinations in LLMs A Quantum Tensor Network Based Method.pdf
papers.file: Semantic Uncertainty Quantification of Hallucinations in LLMs A Quantum Tensor Network Based Method.pdf
papers.title: Semantic Uncertainty Quantification of Hallucinations in LLMs: A Quantum Tensor Network Based Method
papers.summary: Treats the kernel mean embedding of a question's token-sequence (TS) probability distribution as the wave function of a quantum tensor network (QTN), and applies first-order perturbation theory to the QTN's Hamiltonian to quantify the *aleatoric uncertainty of the TS probabilities themselves* (not just their entropy). Uses this per-sample uncertainty signal to recalibrate the probabilities via an entropy-maximization step (balancing Rényi-entropy maximization against a KL penalty scaled inversely by the uncertainty), then computes semantic Rényi entropy over the recalibrated probabilities — the final detector, "SRE-UQ" (denoted SE_R^+). Requires R repeated samples per question (worked example uses R=10) clustered by bidirectional entailment (DeBERTa-large/MNLI), same sampling requirement as Semantic Entropy (Farquhar et al. 2024).
papers.review_connection: A different uncertainty formulation. Keep as literature context unless an exact compatible score can be evaluated on the chosen task.

papers.path: papers/Spectral Top-Down Recovery of Latent Tree Models.pdf
papers.file: Spectral Top-Down Recovery of Latent Tree Models.pdf
papers.title: Spectral Top-Down Recovery of Latent Tree Models
papers.summary: Develops Spectral Top-Down Recovery (STDR), a deterministic divide-and-conquer approach to infer large latent tree graphical models from observed terminal node correlations via low-rank tensor/matrix decompositions.
papers.review_connection: Latent-tree recovery assumes specific structure. Useful for assumptions and possible future models; not proof that current feature families form a valid tree.

papers.path: papers/Spilled Energy in Large Language Models.pdf
papers.file: Spilled Energy in Large Language Models.pdf
papers.title: SPILLED ENERGY IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.summary: Reinterprets the final LLM softmax classifier as an Energy-Based Model (EBM), tracking 'spilled energy' (discrepancies between energy values across consecutive generation steps) directly from output logits as a training-free metric for factual errors and hallucinations.
papers.review_connection: Disambiguate sampled-token NLL from raw-logit energy quantities. Formula and saved-source fidelity matter more than the common “energy” name.

papers.path: papers/Stop When Enough Adaptive Early-Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (ACL 2026).pdf
papers.file: Stop When Enough Adaptive Early-Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (ACL 2026).pdf
papers.title: Stop When Enough: Adaptive Early-Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.summary: REFRAIN is a training-free, one-trace-per-question stopping method with a controller that adapts **across questions**. It stops only after a provisional answer has appeared and the current blank-line-delimited step both contains a reflection cue and is semantically redundant with an earlier step. A sliding-window UCB bandit selects the similarity threshold using an answer-likelihood-minus-length reward.
papers.review_connection: REFRAIN is an adaptive stopping method. Compare actual accuracy and compute under matched generation and closure conventions.

papers.path: papers/Streaming Hallucination Detection in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (arXiv 2601.02170v1).pdf
papers.file: Streaming Hallucination Detection in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (arXiv 2601.02170v1).pdf
papers.title: Streaming Hallucination Detection in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.summary: This is the closest conceptual paper to causal prefix hallucination detection, but it is a **supervised hidden-state probe**, not a label-free logit method or an early-stopping policy. It predicts both whether the current sentence introduces an error and whether the prefix has entered a hallucinated state. The core representation is an L2-normalized, exponentially time-weighted average of token hidden states within the current sentence.
papers.review_connection: Supervised hidden-state prefix/sentence detection. It is not a label-free trace scorer or an actual stopping policy; preserve asset and protocol gaps.

papers.path: papers/The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning.pdf
papers.file: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning.pdf
papers.title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning
papers.summary: Empirical study detailing the development, data synthesis, and evaluation of Process Reward Models (PRMs) for mathematical reasoning. Demonstrates that Monte Carlo estimation-based data synthesis yields inferior generalization compared to LLM-as-a-judge and human supervision.
papers.review_connection: Useful for PRM supervision and step-label construction. Treat PRMs/critics as a distinct access and training tier.

papers.path: papers/TraceDet Hallucination Detection from the Decoding Trace of Diffusion Large Language Models.pdf
papers.file: TraceDet Hallucination Detection from the Decoding Trace of Diffusion Large Language Models.pdf
papers.title: TRACEDET: HALLUCINATION DETECTION FROM THE DECODING TRACE OF DIFFUSION LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.summary: Introduces TraceDet, a hallucination detection framework for Diffusion Large Language Models (D-LLMs) that analyzes the intermediate denoising trajectory ('action trace'). Tracks maximum token entropy across denoising steps to identify unstable generation paths.
papers.review_connection: Diffusion decoding has a different time/denoising axis. It is a conceptual analogy, not an automatic autoregressive trace baseline.

papers.path: papers/Uncertainty Under the Curve A Sequence-Level Entropy Area Metric for Reasoning LLM.pdf
papers.file: Uncertainty Under the Curve A Sequence-Level Entropy Area Metric for Reasoning LLM.pdf
papers.title: Uncertainty Under the Curve: A Sequence-Level Entropy Area Metric for Reasoning LLM
papers.summary: Introduces Entropy Area Score (EAS) / Uncertainty Under the Curve, integrating token-level predictive entropy over the answer generation trajectory without external models or repeated sampling.
papers.review_connection: Sequence entropy area is a simple alternative to richer temporal features. Compare on the same trace, normalization and generation length.

papers.path: papers/Unsupervised Ensemble Learning with Dependent Classifiers.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning with Dependent Classifiers.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning with Dependent Classifiers
papers.summary: Introduces an unsupervised statistical model that allows for dependencies between base classifiers, developing novel unsupervised methods to detect strongly dependent classifiers, estimate their accuracies accurately, and construct an improved meta-learner.
papers.review_connection: The L-SML dependency model motivates grouped fusion. State what is assumed about within-group and across-group errors before claiming theory applies.

papers.path: papers/Unsupervised Ensemble Regression.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Ensemble Regression.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Ensemble Regression
papers.summary: Proposes a framework for unsupervised ensemble regression that estimates unknown continuous responses and detects least/most accurate experts from unlabeled predictions assuming uncorrelated expert deviations.
papers.review_connection: A precursor for combining continuous expert outputs without labels. Check the commensurate-regressor assumptions against heterogeneous uncertainty features.

papers.path: papers/Unsupervised Feature Selection based on Adaptive Similarity Learning and Subspace Clustering.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Feature Selection based on Adaptive Similarity Learning and Subspace Clustering.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection based on Adaptive Similarity Learning and Subspace Clustering
papers.summary: Abstract Feature selection methods have an important role on the readability of data and the reduction of complexity of learning algorithms. In recent years, a variety of eﬀorts are investigated on feature selection problems based on un- supervised viewpoint due to the laborious labeling task on large datasets. In this paper, we propose a novel approach on unsupervised feature selec- tion initiated from the subspace clustering to preserve the similarities by representation learning of low dimensional subspaces among the samples. A self-expressive model is employed to implicitly learn the cluster similarities in an adaptive manner. The proposed method not only maintains the sample similarities through subspace clustering, but it also captures the discrimina- tive information based on a regularized regression model. In line with the convergence analysis of the proposed method, the experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the eﬀectiveness of our approach as com- pared with the state of the art methods. Keywords: Unsupervised feature selection, Graph learning, Subspace clus
papers.review_connection: Another structural objective for feature selection. Low priority after the closed selector cycle unless it introduces a materially new identifiable signal.

papers.path: papers/Unsupervised Feature Selection Through Group Discovery.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Feature Selection Through Group Discovery.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Through Group Discovery (GroupFS)
papers.summary: GroupFS is an end-to-end differentiable, purely-unsupervised feature selector that *jointly* (a) discovers latent groups of related features and (b) selects the most informative groups. It builds two graphs — one over samples, one over features — and enforces Laplacian smoothness on both, plus a group-sparsity regularizer. The signal that distinguishes it from per-feature selectors (LS, DUFS, CAE): informative structure often lives in feature *groups* (adjacent pixels, brain regions, correlated indicators), so it gates whole groups on/off rather than individual features. Ofir Lindenbaum (one of Omri's advisors' orbit) is a co-author; DUFS (Lindenbaum 2021) is the per-feature predecessor.
papers.review_connection: GroupFS jointly studies feature groups and selection. State paper fidelity versus project-specific adaptations and avoid repeating the completed keep-rule sweep.

papers.path: papers/Unsupervised Process Reward Models.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Process Reward Models.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Process Reward Models
papers.summary: uPRM trains a Process Reward Model with **zero human supervision** — no step-level error annotations, no ground-truth final-answer labels. The key mechanism: construct a sequence that interleaves each reasoning step with an explicit correctness marker ("+"/"-"), read the LLM's own next-token probability of emitting that marker, and use this as a training signal. Crucially, **scoring multiple trajectories jointly in one context** (concatenating several marked trajectories together so the LLM sees other trajectories' candidate labels as in-context examples) gives more reliable judgments than scoring each trajectory independently — this joint score is then distilled into a dedicated PRM via LoRA + a custom RL objective (Eq. 12).
papers.review_connection: Full uPRM is a trained process model. A reproduction of its simpler judge baseline does not reproduce uPRM; keep training cost explicit.

papers.path: papers/VICReg Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization.pdf
papers.file: VICReg Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization.pdf
papers.title: VICReg Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Recent self-supervised methods for image representation learning maximize the agreement between embedding vectors produced by encoders fed with different views of the same image. The main challenge is to prevent a collapse in which the encoders produce constant or non-informative vectors. We introduce VICReg (Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization), a method that explicitly avoids the collapse problem with two regularizations terms applied to both embeddings separately: (1) a term that maintains the variance of each embedding dimension above a threshold, (2) a term that decorrelates each pair of variables. Unlike most other approaches to the same problem, VICReg does not require techniques such as: weight sharing between the branches, batch normalization, feature-wise normalization, output quantization, stop gradient, memory banks, etc., and achieves results on par with the state of the art on several downstream tasks. In addition, we show that our variance regularization term stabilizes the training of other methods and leads to performance improvements. 1 INTRODUCTI
papers.review_connection: Variance/covariance regularization prevents collapse; it does not identify correctness. Relevant mainly to a valid new paired-measurement design.

papers.path: papers/Zero-source LLM Hallucination Detection with Human-like Criteria Probing.pdf
papers.file: Zero-source LLM Hallucination Detection with Human-like Criteria Probing.pdf
papers.title: Zero-source LLM Hallucination Detection with Human-like Criteria Probing
papers.summary: Proposes Human-like Criteria Probing for Hallucination Detection (HCPD), an agentic paradigm that emulates multi-perspective human verification criteria to detect hallucinations under strict zero-source constraints (no model internals or external grounding).
papers.review_connection: Human-like criteria probing uses a different verification process. Audit its inference budget and task before numeric comparison.

papers.path: Tenzer2022_Crowdsourcing_Regression_Spectral.pdf
papers.file: Tenzer2022_Crowdsourcing_Regression_Spectral.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Ensemble Regression
papers.summary: Proposes an unsupervised framework for ensemble regression that estimates unknown target responses and detects least/most accurate experts from unlabeled continuous predictions by analyzing prediction covariance moments under uncorrelated error assumptions.
papers.review_connection: This filename contains the older Dror et al. Unsupervised Ensemble Regression paper. Do not cite it as Tenzer 2022; use the correct PMLR source linked above.

papers.path: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning Through Deep Energy-based Models.pdf
papers.file: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning Through Deep Energy-based Models.pdf
papers.title: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning Through Deep Energy-based Models
papers.summary: DEEM is an unsupervised ensemble classifier built from learned multinomial preprocessing layers and a final inverse Restricted Boltzmann Machine (iRBM). The paper proves a bijection between the single-hidden-unit multinomial iRBM and the Dawid–Skene conditional-independence model. The deep layers are intended to transform correlated learner predictions into a representation closer to conditional independence, after which the iRBM estimates the latent class.
papers.review_connection: DEEM is the nonlinear ensemble foundation. Distinguish its published model from the project’s B3 and CIW adapters and from an identifiability guarantee under dependence.
